project.name: House in Erode
project.subtitle: Hacienda + Kerala, abstracted with modern influence
project.climate_note: Inland Tamil Nadu: hot, semi-arid; long dry season, rain mostly from the northeast monsoon (Oct-Dec). Verify against IMD normals before locking the image filter.

en.intro_body: You'll see pairs of pictures. Tap the one you like more. There are no right answers and nothing to explain; go with your first feeling.
en.done_body: That's everything. We'll go through your choices before our next meeting.
en.remote_hint: If you did this remotely, please download your answers and send the file to us.

origins.label: Kerala
origins.description: Kerala vernacular: steep tiled roofs, timber, nalukettu courtyards.

origins.label: Hacienda
origins.description: Spanish-colonial / Latin American hacienda: low terracotta roofs, arcades, patios.

origins.label: Modern
origins.description: Contemporary abstraction: simplified forms, slab, glass, steel, minimal detail.

origins.label: Hybrid / shared
origins.description: Shared by both traditions (e.g. lime whitewash) or already a blend.

dimensions.name: Roof form
dimensions.description: Pitch, eave depth and roofing material, seen from the same angle on a similar house.
dimensions.client_prompt: Which home feels more like yours?
dimensions.isolate_note: Same mass and wall finish, same sky and camera; only the roof changes.

options.label: Steep clay-tile roof
options.description: 35-45° Mangalore-tile roof, deep eaves, gablet vents (mukhappu).
options.why_prompt: What draws you to the steep roof: the silhouette, the deep shade under the eaves, or the tiled texture?

options.label: Low terracotta hip roof
options.description: 15-22° hipped roof in barrel (mission) tile, short eaves, heavy walls below.
options.why_prompt: Is it the lower, calmer roofline you like, or the curved barrel tiles themselves?

options.label: Flat slab, thin overhang
options.description: Flat RCC roof with a thin cantilevered sunshade, usable terrace above.
options.why_prompt: Do you want a usable roof terrace, or is it the clean flat edge you like?

options.label: Single-pitch deep overhang
options.description: Abstracted mono-pitch roof, tile or metal, very deep overhang on slim supports.
options.why_prompt: Is the single slope about looking contemporary, or about one big sheltering overhang?

dimensions.name: Courtyard & massing
dimensions.description: How rooms gather around (or without) open space.
dimensions.client_prompt: Which would you rather live in?
dimensions.isolate_note: Aerial or eye-level views at the same scale and plot size.

options.label: Enclosed nalukettu court
options.description: Four wings around a small open-to-sky nadumuttam; roofs slope inward; verandah ring.
options.why_prompt: What matters most in the enclosed court: privacy, rain falling inside the house, or everyone gathered around one centre?

options.label: Open central patio
options.description: Larger paved patio, arcaded on two to four sides, more sky and sun.
options.why_prompt: Do you picture the patio as an outdoor room for gatherings, or mainly as light and air for the house?

options.label: Linear side court
options.description: Long side garden or slot court along the rooms; rooms open sideways.
options.why_prompt: Is the side court about a garden view from every room, or about keeping the plan compact?

options.label: Compact, no courtyard
options.description: One compact block, light from skylights and terraces instead of a court.
options.why_prompt: You leaned compact: is a courtyard not important to you, or are you worried about cost and upkeep?

dimensions.name: Wall material
dimensions.description: The main wall surface, close up and in daylight.
dimensions.client_prompt: Which would you rather have around you every day?
dimensions.isolate_note: Same window, same light, same crop; only the wall finish changes.

options.label: Exposed laterite
options.description: Cut laterite blocks left exposed, rough and porous, deep red-brown.
options.why_prompt: Is it the colour of laterite you like, or the rough, handmade texture? (Local brick or stone could give either.)

options.label: Lime-plastered whitewash
options.description: Smooth-to-soft lime plaster, whitewashed; shared by both traditions.
options.why_prompt: White walls show every stain in Erode's dust. Is the crisp white essential, or would an off-white lime work?

options.label: Exposed brick
options.description: Wire-cut or country brick, flush or raked joints; contemporary regional.
options.why_prompt: Do you like brick for its warmth, its pattern, or because it needs no painting?

options.label: Hand-troweled stucco
options.description: Thick, hand-troweled plaster with soft edges, earth-tinted.
options.why_prompt: Is it the soft, rounded handmade look, or the warm tint of the plaster?

dimensions.name: Columns & verandah
dimensions.description: The column, bracket and ceiling language of the verandah.
dimensions.client_prompt: Where would you rather sit in the evening?
dimensions.isolate_note: Same verandah depth and floor; columns and ceiling change.

options.label: Timber columns & brackets
options.description: Turned timber posts on stone bases, carved brackets, timber ceiling, built-in seat (charupady).
options.why_prompt: Is it the warmth of the wood, the carved brackets, or the built-in seating along the edge?

options.label: Masonry arcade
options.description: Round-arched plastered arcade on square piers (portales).
options.why_prompt: Is it the arch shape you like, or the solid, shaded rhythm of a deep arcade?

options.label: Slim iron posts & rails
options.description: Slim wrought-iron posts, corbels and railings, timber beam above.
options.why_prompt: Do you like the ironwork as ornament, or for how light and open it keeps the verandah?

options.label: Slender steel/RCC frame
options.description: Thin steel or RCC columns, flat soffit, no ornament.
options.why_prompt: Is the plain frame about a clean look, or about less maintenance than timber?

dimensions.name: Windows & openings
dimensions.client_prompt: Which would you rather look out of?
dimensions.isolate_note: Same wall, same room behind; only the opening changes.

options.label: Rectangular timber slat windows
options.description: Rectilinear timber frames, louvred shutters, vertical bars.
options.why_prompt: Do you like being able to open everything for breeze, or the filtered light through the slats?

options.label: Arched openings, iron grilles
options.description: Arched heads, deep reveals, decorative iron grilles (rejas).
options.why_prompt: Is it the arch shape, or the deep, thick-walled reveal around the window?

options.label: Full-height shaded glazing
options.description: Floor-to-ceiling glazing behind deep shade or screens.
options.why_prompt: Big glass in Erode's sun needs deep shade. Which room do you picture this in, and facing which way?

options.label: Brick or terracotta jaali
options.description: Perforated brick or terracotta screen walls filtering light and air.
options.why_prompt: Is the jaali about privacy from the street, or the pattern of light it throws inside?

dimensions.name: Colour & palette
dimensions.description: Overall colour mood of the house, indoors and out.
dimensions.isolate_note: Similar rooms or facades; colour is what differs.

options.label: Ochre & terracotta warmth
options.description: Warm ochre walls, terracotta floors, deep blue or green painted accents.
options.why_prompt: Is it the warmth you want, or the colourful accents (blue, green, tiles)?

options.label: Natural wood & whitewash
options.description: Dark natural timber, white lime walls, red-oxide floors.
options.why_prompt: Is it the restraint (few colours), or the contrast of dark wood against white?

options.label: Muted earth & stone
options.description: Sand, grey granite, concrete, muted greens.
options.why_prompt: Do you want calm, low-contrast colour throughout, or a neutral base to add colour to later?

dimensions.inactive_note: Off: colour warmth and ornament are read from the hidden tags on every photo in the other sets.

dimensions.name: Landscape & threshold
dimensions.description: Planting, water and how the verandah meets the garden.
dimensions.client_prompt: Which would you rather step out into?
dimensions.isolate_note: Same verandah edge; the planting and water change.

options.label: Courtyard planting, tulsi thara
options.description: Small planted court with a tulsi thara, frangipani, open verandah edges.
options.why_prompt: Is the planted court about a ritual centre for the family, or simply greenery you can see from every room?

options.label: Tiled fountain patio
options.description: Central tiled fountain or water channel, paving, potted plants.
options.why_prompt: Is it the sound of water, the decorative tile, or a paved space for gatherings?

options.label: Lush tropical garden
options.description: Verandah opening straight onto a dense green garden (banana, heliconia, palms).
options.why_prompt: A lush garden needs a lot of water in Erode. How much maintenance and irrigation are you willing to take on?

options.label: Dry native garden, shade trees
options.description: Climate-native planting, gravel, boulders, neem or pongamia shade.
options.why_prompt: Do you like the dry garden's look, or is it about low water and low upkeep?

options.label: Minimal reflecting pool
options.description: Shallow still water edged in stone, sparse planting.
options.why_prompt: Is the still water about calm and reflection, or about cooling the air near the verandah?

dimensions.name: Modern abstraction
dimensions.description: How much traditional detail to keep: ornate, restrained, minimal.
dimensions.isolate_note: Same subject (e.g. a verandah) drawn at different levels of detail.

options.label: Ornate, full traditional detail
options.description: Carved brackets, mouldings, decorative tile and ironwork kept.
options.why_prompt: Which ornaments matter to you, and which are just part of the overall feeling?

options.label: Restrained, simplified traditional
options.description: Traditional forms kept, ornament reduced to a few key pieces.
options.why_prompt: If we keep only two or three traditional pieces, which would they be?

options.label: Minimal, abstracted
options.description: Only the essence: proportion, shade, material; no ornament.
options.why_prompt: With no ornament, what should still tell people this house is rooted in tradition?

dimensions.inactive_note: Off: colour warmth and ornament are read from the hidden tags on every photo in the other sets.

brief.title: A few practical questions
brief.intro: Optional, but it helps us connect what you liked to how you live.

fields.label: Who will live in the house?
fields.placeholder: e.g. the two of us, two children, my parents on weekends

fields.label: Which spaces must the house have?
How many cars should be parked under cover?
Anything you definitely want?
fields.placeholder: e.g. a courtyard with rain falling in, a big verandah swing

fields.label: Anything you definitely don't want?
fields.placeholder: e.g. no dark rooms, no high maintenance garden

fields.label: Do you know the plot yet?

tensions.prompt: You liked the enclosed nalukettu court and the low hacienda roof. A nalukettu traditionally depends on steep roofs draining into the court. Was it the enclosure you liked, or the rain falling inside?
You chose a flat roof but timber verandah columns. Should the timber carry the tradition while the roof stays modern, or does the roof feel unfinished without tiles?
You liked full-height glass. In Erode's heat it needs deep shade: which rooms do you picture opening up fully, and which way would they face?
You chose the lush garden. It needs a lot of irrigation through Erode's dry months. Would a dense planted courtyard with a smaller dry garden outside give you the same feeling?
You chose minimal detail overall but liked the carved timber verandah. Which one or two traditional pieces are worth keeping in a minimal house?
You liked white lime walls but an ochre-terracotta palette. Should the walls stay white with the warmth in floors and roofs, or should the walls themselves be tinted?
You leaned towards a compact house without a courtyard, but liked the planted courtyard garden. Is a small court worth the extra footprint?

values.open: spaces open to sky and garden
values.compact: a compact house with no court
